name: Parecoxib
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Parecoxib is an injectable prodrug of the cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitor valdecoxib. Valdecoxib clearance is unchanged even in severe kidney impairment and dialysis, and it is not removed by hemodialysis, but COX-2 inhibition can cause fluid retention and acute kidney failure. The European label needs no change at creatinine clearance (CrCl) 30–80 mL/min and starts at 20 mg with close kidney monitoring below 30 mL/min. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: European summary of product characteristics (SmPC) uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min); thresholds 80 and 30.

bands.recommendation: Usual: 40 mg IV or IM, then 20 or 40 mg every 6 to 12 hours as needed; maximum 80 mg/day; limited experience beyond 3 days (SmPC).
CrCl 30–80: no dose adjustment (SmPC). Rehydrate before starting; caution with diuretics, ACE inhibitors or ARBs.
CrCl <30 (severe) or prone to fluid retention: start at the lowest dose, 20 mg, and monitor kidney function closely (SmPC).
Start at 20 mg and monitor kidney function closely (SmPC). NSAID risk to remaining kidney function; use only if clearly needed.

hd: Valdecoxib clearance is unchanged on dialysis and it is not removed by hemodialysis; SmPC severe-impairment rule (start 20 mg, monitor) applies. Weigh residual kidney function.
pd: Severe-impairment rule (start 20 mg, monitor) applies; NSAIDs can reduce residual kidney function.
crrt: No CRRT data. COX-2 inhibitors can worsen acute kidney injury; avoid if possible.
dialyzable: No: valdecoxib is not removed by hemodialysis (about 98% protein-bound) (SmPC).
monitoring: Kidney function closely at CrCl <30 or with fluid retention; blood pressure, edema; INR with anticoagulants; lithium levels (SmPC 4.2, 4.4, 4.5).
